QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_64

question.text: SAS-1300 distinguishes "access" from "usage" of financial products. Which set of metrics BEST captures USAGE rather than just access?

answer.text: Branch count in the project area
Participants using bank accounts, ATM cards, mobile and netbanking and online payment apps, with a measurable shift from cash or non-formal sources to formal and digital transactions

explanation.text: The Logic: The E-Diksha pages support bank-account use, ATM-card use, mobile and netbanking, online payment apps, and a shift from cash or non-formal sources to formal or digital transactions as the usage-side measures. These indicators capture whether the products are actually being used, not just whether they have been made available. The Trap: Accounts opened (A), branch count (B) and ATM cards issued (C) describe access or supply-side coverage; they do not show whether the products are being used. Note: Frame usage indicators in source terms - participants using bank accounts, ATM cards, mobile banking, netbanking and online payment apps, and the shift towards digital and formal transactions - rather than inventing transaction-frequency thresholds that are not in the source.
